title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering + fallback for regional failover
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: During a regional outage last week we observed ordering anomalies in the SLO enforcer backoff path that caused inconsistent circuit-breaker state transitions and, in some cases, aggressive load-shedding of healthy regions. This PR stabilizes the backoff ordering logic and adds a deterministic fallback path to ensure regional failover doesn't cause split-brain behavior. Root cause: race between the backoff hysteresis updater and the regional-failover coordinator when both attempted to adjust queue priorities and CB state concurrently. The result was non-deterministic ordering of fallback operations and a cascade of premature load-shedding. What this PR changes: 1) Serialize state transitions for the SLO enforcer using a lightweight state-machine lock: slo/enforcer/state_machine.go (adds state guard and ordered transition queue). 2) Add deterministic fallback policy: slo/enforcer/fallback_policy.go (policy picks highest-capacity healthy region and enqueues a single fallback request; prevents parallel fallbacks). 3) Fix ordering of backoff/hysteresis updates to be applied after routing decisions are computed to avoid preemptive shedding. 4) Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent backoff + failover operations (slo/enforcer/*_test.go). 5) Instrumentation: metrics and spans to make ordering visible in traces (observability/slo_enforcer_ordering). Rollout plan: hotfix branch -> canary on a low-traffic region for 2 hours -> staged rollout to other regions with monitoring on SLO violations and circuit-breaker open rates. Rollback plan: revert merge and redeploy previous enforcer binary; feature flag is present (slo.enforcer.stabilize_backoff=true) to toggle the new behaviour quickly. Testing: local unit tests + integration job simulating failover (ran in CI); load test in perf-canary environment (1M requests/hour) validated no regression in p95 latency and reduced CB thrash. Related work: ENG-54321 (incident postmortem), SUP-2345 (customer-facing support ticket), ENG-54600 (follow-up observability work).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can we guarantee the state-machine guard won't be a contention hotspot under high QPS? Please add benchmark results.
Aisha Patel: Added microbenchmarks in state_machine_test.go showing <2% throughput regression at 2k RPS per enforcer; contention occurs only when failovers are triggered, which is expected.

Priya Shah: The fallback selection looks reasonable but we need to ensure KMS/secret access isn't blocked during regional failover paths. Also add a guard to avoid retries when region metadata is stale.
Aisha Patel: Guard added (region_selector.go) to reject stale metadata and a retry backoff with jitter. Added note to runbook.
Liam O'Brien: CI flaky on integration test first run (timing). Re-ran CI; all checks passed on second run. Approving for merge after tiny docs wording fix.
Priya Shah: Approve after verifying perf-canary metrics and observing reduced CB open/close churn during simulated failover.
release_notes:
- Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering to prevent premature load-shedding during regional failover.
- Add deterministic fallback policy to avoid concurrent fallback operations and reduce circuit-breaker thrashing.
- Fix ordering of backoff/hysteresis updates to apply after routing decisions.
- Added tests and observability for ordering and fallback events.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag slo.enforcer.stabilize_backoff=true included. Canary rollout recommended. Watch metrics: slo.enforcer.slo_violation_rate, slo.enforcer.cb_open_rate, slo.enforcer.fallback_count. If regressions observed, flip feature flag and redeploy previous release.
post_merge_actions: Monitor canary for 4 hours and promote if stable
Create ENG follow-up (ENG-54600) to add trace-based alerting for ordering anomalies
Notify on-call SRE and customers referenced in SUP-2345
